proposals.evidence: DEDR 1 full article: Ka. a- remote demonstrative base; ava/āta, avaḷ/āke, avar/avargaḷ, adu/atu/attu, avu that man, that woman, those persons, that thing, those things; adj. ā; ako, agō˘, adē̆, adō behold!; añce on that side,… The article gives Kannada avar “they”; Census avaratu is a possessive form of that distal plural.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 3647 full article: Ka. nāvu ( obl. nam- ) we (inclusive) (in Old Ka.; G. S. Gai, Bull. Deccan College Research Institute I. 411 f.); we (in mod. Ka.). Tu. nama we (inclusive). Te. manamu ( obl. mana- ) id. Kol. ne·nḍ id. Nk.… The article gives Kannada nāvu with oblique nam- “we”; Census nāmu keeps that inclusive-plural stem.

proposals.evidence: DEDR 5151 full article: Ka. yā-, ā-, ē-, e- interrogative base; yā, yāva, ā, āva, dāva, ē, e what, which; yār, ār, dāru who ( pl. ); yāvanu, āvaṃ, āve which man; yāvaḷu, āvaḷ which woman; āvudu what, which; pl. āvuvu; yāke, yātake,… The article gives Kannada ēn “what”; Census ēnā retains the interrogative stem.
